task.description:
This is WF-03 Step 5 (Close Issue). The root cause IS removed: Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' child spec is now restart: :temporary, so the top-level Letflow.Supervisor structurally can never auto-restart it under any fault duration (proven, not merely bounded, per lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md section 4 -- 0 restarts consumed from the top-level's own budget, unconditionally); a new Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker becomes sole restart authority and trips to a stopped :open state after 2 consecutive exits, backing off exponentially rather than crash-looping forever. This was proven correct via a new fail-then-pass mutation-tested regression test (test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs), independently re-verified by TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (one mutant independently reproduced), and the full suite (mix letflow.check.test) is green at 3203+7+11 passed, 0 failures. All prior gates (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR x3 rework cycles, SECURITY-REVIEWER, REVIEWER) PASSED. This is the normal terminal state -- status: resolved.

Update docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml per ISSUE_QUEUE.md's status vocabulary for 'resolved': set status: resolved, add resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0451-20260904, resolved_at: <real UTC timestamp>. Then close the GitHub issue (github_issue: 865 per the yaml's existing field) with `gh issue close 865 --comment "Fixed in WF03-ISS0451-20260904. See docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml and the regression test at test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs."` -- this comment text is mandatory per ISSUE_QUEUE.md's 'resolved' branch, do not omit it or close without it.
acceptance_criteria: docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml status: resolved, with resolved_in_run:/resolved_at: keys (not verdict_in_run:/verdict_at:, which are for no_defect only)
gh issue close 865 run with the exact --comment text specified (or the ISSUE_QUEUE.md-equivalent wording), citing the run-id, the issue yaml, and the regression test path
Handoff result confirms both the local yaml write and the GitHub close succeeded, or explains explicitly if gh was unavailable
